content: Efavirenz is a medication prescribed to treat human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection in combination with other medications. It is used in patients with or without acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). Efavirenz belongs to a class of drugs known as non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). It works by slowing the spread of HIV within the body. However, it does not cure HIV infection, nor does it prevent the development of HIV-related illnesses or the transmission of HIV to others. Efavirenz is available in capsule and tablet forms, taken orally. It is typically taken once daily with plenty of water on an empty stomach, preferably at the same time each day. Taking it at bedtime may help reduce bothersome side effects. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Even if you feel well, continue taking efavirenz as directed. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. If your supply is running low, ensure you obtain more from your doctor or pharmacist. Missing doses or stopping the medication can make your condition harder to treat. Efavirenz is also used in combination with another medication to help prevent HIV infection in healthcare workers or others who have been accidentally exposed to the virus. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking efavirenz, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to efavirenz or any other medications. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and nutritional supplements you are taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as those for anxiety, mental illness, pain, seizures, or HIV/AIDS, may interact with efavirenz, requiring dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects. Inform your doctor about any herbal products you are using, especially those containing kava or St. John’s wort. If you consume large amounts of alcohol, use street drugs, or have a history of seizures, high cholesterol, mental illness, or heart, liver, or pancreas disease, let your doctor know. Women should not become pregnant while taking efavirenz. A negative pregnancy test is required before starting the medication, and effective birth control must be used during treatment. Efavirenz may interfere with hormonal contraceptives, so a barrier method (e.g., condoms or diaphragms) should be used in addition to other birth control methods. Consult your doctor to choose the most suitable method. If you become pregnant while taking efavirenz, contact your doctor immediately, as it may harm the fetus. Breastfeeding is not recommended for women infected with HIV or those taking efavirenz. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking efavirenz. Be aware that efavirenz may cause drowsiness, dizziness, or difficulty concentrating. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as it can worsen efavirenz’s side effects. Note that your body fat may increase or redistribute to areas such as the breasts or upper back. Efavirenz may also cause changes in thoughts, behavior, or mental health. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms such as depression, suicidal thoughts, aggressive behavior, hallucinations, or loss of touch with reality. Ensure your family is aware of these symptoms so they can seek help on your behalf if necessary. Consult your doctor about consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while taking efavirenz. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Efavirenz may cause side effects. Common side effects include upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, indigestion, drowsiness, dizziness, headache, difficulty concentrating, confusion, forgetfulness, nervousness, strange thoughts, unusually happy mood, difficulty sleeping, unusual dreams, and pain. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects include sore throat, cough, fever, chills, rash, itching, blisters, peeling skin, fainting, extreme tiredness, lack of energy, loss of appetite, upper right stomach pain, unusual bleeding or bruising, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, and seizures. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms or those mentioned in the special precautions section. Report serious side effects to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store efavirenz in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include uncontrollable body movements, dizziness, headache, difficulty concentrating, nervousness, confusion, forgetfulness, difficulty sleeping, unusual dreams, drowsiness, hallucinations, unusually happy mood, and strange thoughts. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to efavirenz. Inform laboratory personnel that you are taking efavirenz before undergoing any tests. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
